AWPTCM-T33303.objective:
• An Ethernet interface configured as a tagged member of one or more VLANs transmits frames for those VLANs with an 802.1Q tag carrying the matching VID.
  • Frames received on a tagged interface bearing a VID for which that interface is a tagged member are classified into that VLAN and forwarded within it.
  • A single interface simultaneously holds untagged membership of one VLAN and tagged membership of one or more other VLANs, with each membership operating independently.
  • Untagged and priority-tagged frames received on an interface are classified into that interface's native/untagged VLAN.
  • Frames egressing an interface on its native/untagged VLAN leave with no VLAN tag, and the tag is removed on egress when the ingressing frame was tagged with the native VID.
  • The native/untagged VLAN of an interface is changeable, and after a change ingress classification and egress untagged transmission both follow the new native VID.
  • The same VID is configurable as a tagged member on two or more separate interfaces, and those interfaces form a single forwarding domain for that VID.
  • Tagged frames traverse a bridge between two tagged interfaces of the same VLAN with the VID, priority and payload preserved end to end.
  • Traffic in one VLAN remains isolated from interfaces that hold no membership of that VLAN, whether tagged or untagged.
  • An interface belonging to both a protocol-based VLAN and a tagged VLAN forwards each frame into the VLAN selected by the applicable classification rule, with protocol-template matching taking effect for untagged and priority-tagged frames.
  • The VID Set for a port associates each Protocol Group Identifier with a VID, and an untagged or priority-tagged frame matching a Protocol Template is assigned the corresponding VID.
  • Removal of all VLAN tagged memberships from an interface is possible, after which the interface carries only its untagged VLAN and drops or discards frames tagged with the removed VIDs.
  • An interface with no remaining VLAN membership passes no user traffic.
  • VID 0 (priority-tagged) frames received on an access/untagged interface are forwarded in the interface's untagged VLAN rather than discarded.
  • Ethernet interfaces enslaved to the global bridge default to untagged membership of VID 1 and tagged membership of all other configured VLANs in the range 2..4094.
  • Boundary VIDs (lowest and highest valid values) are configurable as tagged memberships and forward traffic identically to mid-range VIDs.
  • Configuration of a reserved or out-of-range VID on an interface is rejected with a clear error and leaves existing VLAN membership unchanged.
  • Tagging configuration for a VLAN that does not exist is either rejected or held inactive, and does not create silent forwarding for that VID.
  • Conflicting membership requests on one interface (for example two untagged VLANs) are rejected, with the prior valid state retained.
  • Frames tagged with a VID for which the ingress interface has no membership are discarded and are not leaked into any other VLAN.
  • Double-tagged or malformed 802.1Q frames arriving on a tagged interface are handled deterministically, with no forwarding into an unintended VLAN and no impact on interface stability.
  • VLAN membership and tagged/untagged status per interface are reportable, and the reported state matches the configured state.
  • The untagged set for each VLAN is reportable as the entries in the port map specifying untagged transmission.
  • Per-VLAN and per-interface frame counters increment consistently with the tagged and untagged traffic actually forwarded.
  • MAC addresses learned from tagged traffic appear in the forwarding database against the VID carried in the tag.
  • Tagging configuration persists across interface link transitions, VLAN reconfiguration and device restart, with forwarding behaviour resuming unchanged.
  • Changes to tagged membership take effect without disrupting traffic on the interface's other VLANs.
  • Rejected tagging operations and discarded frames are observable through logs or counters sufficient to distinguish a misconfiguration from a forwarding fault.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Create multiple VLANs on the device and set an Ethernet interface as a tagged member of two or more of them, leaving its untagged VLAN at the default.
Verify frames transmitted by the interface for each VLAN of which it is a tagged member egress with an 802.1Q tag carrying the matching VID.
Test with tagged frames received on the interface bearing a VID for which that interface is a tagged member, and confirm they are classified into that VLAN and forwarded within it.
Set a single interface to hold untagged membership of one VLAN and tagged membership of one or more other VLANs simultaneously, and confirm each membership operates independently.
Test with untagged frames received on the interface and confirm they are classified into that interface's native/untagged VLAN.
Test with priority-tagged frames received on the interface and confirm they are also classified into the native/untagged VLAN.
Verify frames egressing the interface on its native/untagged VLAN leave with no VLAN tag.
Test with frames ingressing tagged with the native VID and confirm the tag is removed on egress from the untagged member interface.
Change the native/untagged VLAN of the interface to a different VID and confirm the change is accepted.
Verify that after the native VLAN change, ingress classification of untagged frames follows the new native VID.
Verify that after the native VLAN change, untagged egress transmission follows the new native VID.
Set the same VID as a tagged member on two or more separate interfaces and confirm those interfaces form a single forwarding domain for that VID.
Test with tagged frames traversing the bridge between two tagged interfaces of the same VLAN and confirm the VID, priority and payload are preserved end to end.
Verify traffic in one VLAN remains isolated from interfaces that hold no membership of that VLAN, whether tagged or untagged.
Set an interface as a member of both a protocol-based VLAN and a tagged VLAN, and confirm each frame is forwarded into the VLAN selected by the applicable classification rule.
Test with untagged and priority-tagged frames matching a Protocol Template and confirm protocol-template matching takes effect for those frames.
Verify the VID Set for a port associates each Protocol Group Identifier with a VID, and that an untagged or priority-tagged frame matching a Protocol Template is assigned the corresponding VID.
Remove all VLAN tagged memberships from an interface and confirm the interface carries only its untagged VLAN.
Test with frames tagged with the removed VIDs and confirm they are dropped or discarded on that interface.
Remove all remaining VLAN membership from an interface and confirm it passes no user traffic.
Test with VID 0 (priority-tagged) frames received on an access/untagged interface and confirm they are forwarded in the interface's untagged VLAN rather than discarded.
Verify Ethernet interfaces enslaved to the global bridge default to untagged membership of VID 1 and tagged membership of all other configured VLANs in the range 2..4094.
Set the lowest and highest valid VIDs as tagged memberships on an interface and confirm traffic is forwarded identically to a mid-range VID.
Test with a reserved or out-of-range VID configured on an interface and confirm the request is rejected with a clear error.
Confirm the interface's existing VLAN membership is unchanged after the rejected VID configuration.
Test with tagging configuration applied for a VLAN that does not exist and confirm it is either rejected or held inactive, creating no silent forwarding for that VID.
Test with conflicting membership requests on one interface, for example two untagged VLANs, and confirm the request is rejected and the prior valid state is retained.
Test with frames tagged with a VID for which the ingress interface has no membership and confirm they are discarded and not leaked into any other VLAN.

Test with double-tagged and malformed 802.1Q frames arriving on a tagged interface and confirm handling is deterministic, with no forwarding into an unintended VLAN and no impact on interface stability.
Verify VLAN membership and tagged/untagged status per interface are reportable and the reported state matches the configured state.
Verify the untagged set for each VLAN is reportable as the entries in the port map specifying untagged transmission.
Verify per-VLAN and per-interface frame counters increment consistently with the tagged and untagged traffic actually forwarded.
Verify MAC addresses learned from tagged traffic appear in the forwarding database against the VID carried in the tag.
Verify tagging configuration and forwarding behaviour persist unchanged across an interface link down and link up transition.
Verify tagging configuration persists across VLAN reconfiguration and a device restart, with forwarding behaviour resuming unchanged.
Change tagged membership on an interface while traffic is running and confirm traffic on the interface's other VLANs is not disrupted.
Verify rejected tagging operations and discarded frames are observable through logs or counters sufficient to distinguish a misconfiguration from a forwarding fault.
